sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.4967 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A1 to A5 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.277 of 2019 of Kancharapalem Police Station, Viakhapatnam City, which was registered against them for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273 r/w 34 IPC, Section 7(1) r/w 20(1) of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce,
Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (for short, 'COTP Act, 2003') and Sections 48, 59 and 63 of Food Safety Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').
2.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce,
Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 23.06.2019 at 17.30 hours, the complainant on receiving the credible information proceeded to Gnanapuram Railway Station Parcel Office, and seized two autos bearing Nos.AP 31TF 2645 and AP 31TF 4302 used for transporting banned tobacco products and also arrested the accused and on interrogation, they came to know that they were selling the Gutka Packets to pan shops at higher prices.
Hence, the FIR is registered for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273 r/w 34 IPC, Section 7(1) r/w 20(1) of COTP Act, 2003 and Sections 48, 59 and 63 of FSS Act.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, the Gutka which is a tobacco product would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of Food Safety Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act') and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime and investigate and file charge sheet and therefore,
registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.

As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and only quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act, whereas permitted the respondents to proceed against the petitioners therein for the offences punishable under the provisions of COTP Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto basing on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police of Kancharapalem Police Station.

Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned I.Kondala Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 11 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101894196/
1 and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.
5.

sentences.text: Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is partly allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners under Sections 188, 272, 273 r/w 34 IPC and Sections 48, 59 and 63 of FSS Act are hereby quashed and the respondents are permitted to proceed against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Section 7(1) r/w 20(1) of COTP Act, 2003.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.

U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J 11.09.2019 SS I.Kondala Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 11 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101894196/
